ONE GENERIC GSETTINGS SERVICE (batch B0), plus dedicated D-Bus methods per domain. Every write follows host/src/services/system/energy.rs. No new crates: the build stays --offline --locked. C libraries are opened with dlopen, using the bindings! pattern of host/src/files/archive_ffi.rs, which B0 lifts into host/src/dlib.rs. They are libpulse.so.0, libcups.so.2, libqrencode.so.4, libcanberra.so.0, libpwquality.so.1, libcrypt.so.1 and libgoa-backend-1.0.so.2. A missing library means that feature reports unavailable.

1. gsettings.* (host/src/services/gsettings.rs, prefix gsettings.)
- gsettings.get {keys:[{schema, key, path?}]}
  - Returns {items:[{schema, path, key, allowed, available, writable, owned, value, default, isDefault, type, range}]}.
  - The schema comes from SettingsSchemaSource::default().lookup(id, true). A missing schema gives available:false. writable is is_writable (lockdown). range is enum names, flag names or min/max.
- gsettings.set {schema, path?, values:{key: value}}, dangerous
  - Takes one or more keys of the same schema and path, all checked before anything is queued.
  - Each key must be allowlisted and in Write mode, have the right type, pass range_check, and be writable.
  - Then delay, set_value, apply, Settings::sync and a read-back of every key. A mismatch is failed (notTaken).
  - ctx.dry_run validates only.
- gsettings.reset {schema, path?, keys}, dangerous.
- Event gsettings.changed {schema, path, key, item}.
  - It comes from connect_changed and connect_writable_changed on every schema the service has opened.
  - The watchers live on the service's own GLib MainContext thread, as system.rs does.
- JSON to GVariant follows the key's type:
  - b, i, u, q, d, s, as, ai, ad, a(ss), (dd)
  - enum becomes a string, flags an array of strings
  - other types are refused
- Allowlist: host/src/services/gsettings/allow/{input, devices, network, system, accounts, apps}.rs, one file per batch. Each is a const table of Allow {schema, keys, path, mode}.
  - path is a relocatable pattern with typed holes: {appid} [a-z0-9-]{1,128}, {custom} custom[0-9]{1,4}, {vidpid} [0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{4}, {serial} [0-9a-f]{1,16}, {button} button[A-Z], {service} [a-z-]{1,32}.
  - mode is one of Write, Read, or Owned(winpoint setting path).
  - B0 fills all six files from the page table of this plan. A batch edits only its own file.
- Refusals, all with nl/en texts in host/i18n/gsettings.tsv:
  - Not allowlisted: denied gsettings.notAllowed.
  - Owned by WinPoint's look: denied gsettings.ownedByWinPoint, with data.setting, so the page links to the WinPoint control. These are the keys written through gnome_look::note: color-scheme, gtk-theme, icon-theme, accent-color, button-layout, and every org.gnome.desktop.background key.
  - Held by the extension: the media-keys logout key, and any wm.keybindings key recorded in the extension's logout-restore or task-view-restore. This check is dynamic.
  - Locked: denied gsettings.locked.
  - Type or range wrong: bad_args gsettings.badValue.
  - Schema missing: unsupported gsettings.unavailable.
- The allowlist never contains ubuntu-dock, DING or tiling-assistant schemas, and never org.gnome.shell enabled-extensions or mutter experimental-features. A test asserts this.

- B0 adds common::call_interactive.

  - NotAuthorized and Cancelled map to denied with core.notAuthorized or core.authCancelled.

Dock on/off, auto-hide, panel mode, icon size, show on, position, show volumes / unmounted / network volumes and show trash. Enhanced Tiling on/off, tiling popup and tile groups. These configure ubuntu-dock, DING and tiling-assistant, which the WinPoint session never loads: /usr/share/gnome-shell/modes/winpoint.json enables only win11-gnome. WinPoint's taskbar, desktop icons and snap replace them (Taakbalk, Bureaubladpictogrammen, Multitasking). Writing those keys would only change the Ubuntu session.

Multitasking › monitor isolation (dash-to-dock isolate-monitors), and the Ubuntu patch's extra write of tiling-assistant tiling-popup-all-workspace with App Switching: same reason, Ubuntu Dock and tiling-assistant only. The current-workspace-only key itself is kept.

Multitasking › Reopen Windows After Login (org.gnome.desktop.session save-restore): its group is visible=false in GNOME 50's own UI, so it is not a working GNOME function. It returns under Aanmeldingsopties if GNOME shows it again.

Sharing › File Sharing (WebDAV, Public folder, Require Password, Password, networks) and Bluetooth file receiving: both need gnome-user-share, which is not installed, and GNOME hides the rows too. They would go to Geavanceerde instellingen voor delen and Apparaten once it is installed.

Users › Parental Controls, the Wellbeing Parental Controls banner and the malcontent app-list filter in Apps: malcontent-control is not installed and GNOME hides them. Their Windows place would be Accounts › Familie.
Users › Add Enterprise Login (realmd / adcli): not installed and hidden by GNOME. Its Windows place would be Accounts › Toegang tot werk of school.
Privacy › Telemetry › Automatic Error Reporting (ABRT): Fedora only. There is no ABRT service on Ubuntu and GNOME hides the row. Ubuntu's whoopsie and ubuntu-insights rows are kept.
Color › printer calibration and View Details (gcm-viewer): they need gnome-color-manager, which is not installed, and GNOME hides those buttons. Display calibration with a sensor is kept.

Printers › driver lookup through system-config-printer's D-Bus service (GetBestDrivers, GroupPhysicalDevices, MissingExecutables): scp-dbus-service is a Python program, and WinPoint may not run Python. Driver choice stays, through CUPS's own PPD list and driverless IPP Everywhere. Only the missing-executables check is gone.
About › Support GNOME / Donate: hidden in GNOME's own UI (visible=false), donation reminder off on Ubuntu, and not a setting.
Appearance › OLED hint: a label that is hidden in GNOME's UI. It is informational only.

testing:
RULES
- Nothing ever runs against Robin's live session: no gsettings, dconf, gdbus or busctl, no live buses.
- Heavy work goes through tools/heavy.sh and its .heavy.lock. Harness runs queue behind each other, so the batches' runs are serialised. Use one cargo target dir per worktree (WIN11_CARGO_TARGET_DIR).

UNIT TESTS, every batch
- Host: tests/rust-sandbox/run-tests.sh --lib (keyfile GSettings, private session bus, unreachable system bus, guard-bin stubs).
- Native workspace: cargo test, plus tests/i18n (test_native.py checks that settings_pages.json equals the registry; check_rust / check_native; the glossary; no Dutch words in en).

B0 unit tests
- Allowlist audit:
  - every entry's schema is installed (or marked optional: tracker, ubuntu, whoopsie, remote-desktop) and every key exists with the type its mapping expects;
  - relocatable entries are checked through the schema id;
  - no ubuntu-dock, ding or tiling-assistant schema and no enabled-extensions or experimental-features in Write mode;
  - every gnome_look key is Owned.
- JSON ↔ GVariant round trips for every supported type, enum and flag. Unknown types are refused.
- Memory backend: set, read back, reset, multi-key atomic set. A keyfile backend with a locks file gives denied. Wrong type or range gives bad_args. dry_run writes nothing.
- gsettings.changed fires for an external write.
- Extension-held keys are refused, from a fixture extension schema.
- Mirror: both directions with a temporary settings.json and the memory backend; no loop; accent-color goes through gnome_look::note and --gnome-look restores it.
- caps parses fixture /sys and /run/udev trees.
- api-methods fragments: no duplicates. Every name in every service's METHODS table is listed, and every mutating one is dangerous.
- Registry:
  - every id has a builder;
  - parent chains are acyclic and at most three deep;
  - needs keys are known to caps;
  - breadcrumbs for third-level pages;
  - search: nl 'muis' and en 'mouse' find mouse first; 'touchpad', 'printer', 'vpn', 'proxy', 'nachtlampje' → nightlight, 'toetsenbord', 'sneltoetsen' and 'vergrootglas' resolve; a needs-filtered page is hidden.

Per-batch unit tests
- Pure parsers on fixtures, or on the installed files with a skip when absent:
  - A: evdev.xml, ibus components, the keybinding XMLs, libwacom .tablet files.
  - B: IPP and PPD responses, the bolt and colord dict decoders.
  - C: the NM settings map (round trip keeps unknown keys), serviceproviders.xml, the WIFI: QR string.
  - D: GetCurrentState decode and ApplyMonitorsConfig encode, night-light strength ↔ Kelvin, pulse volume and balance math.
  - E: passwd PTY transcript states, crypt prefix, zone labels, the pkg_depends parser.
  - F: search-provider .ini, flatpak metadata, the snapd HTTP client against a socketpair, consent files.
- Value mappings: mouse 1-20 ↔ -1..1, touchpad 1-10, cursor sizes, lock-delay options, old-files-age presets.
- Every method's dry-run path writes nothing.
- D-Bus-backed methods run as #[ignore] bus tests inside tests/dbus-fakes/run.sh. That is B0's generalisation of the tests/update/run.sh bwrap layer: private system and session bus, stubs first on PATH, strace on connect. Fakes per batch go under tests/dbus-fakes/fakes/<batch>/:
  - A: none needed beyond the extension.
  - B: BlueZ Adapter1, UPower devices, bolt, colord, CupsPkHelper and Avahi; libcups talks to tests/gnome/lib/fake_ipp.py on loopback through CUPS_SERVER.
  - C: NetworkManager with settings, secrets, devices and active connections; ModemManager; gsd Sharing; org.gnome.RemoteDesktop; systemd1.
  - D: Mutter DisplayConfig is real in the harness; gsd Color; UPower.
  - E: AccountsService, fprintd, hostname1, timedate1, timesync1, locale1, GOA, PackageKit.
  - F: PermissionStore, WhoopsiePreferences, fwupd, GlobalShortcutsRebind.
- Each fake records its calls, and the test compares them with what the page action must send, including interactive=true and the ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION flag.

GNOME HARNESS (tests/gnome/harness.py)
- A private headless GNOME Shell 50 at 1440×900, with private keyfile GSettings at run/config/glib-2.0/settings/keyfile. Its private buses have no services, so the stand-ins come from tests/gnome/lib/standins.py, started by the scenario on the private system or session bus, as winpoint-update.py and native-gtk-apps.py do today.
- One scenario per batch: settings-input.py, settings-a11y.py, settings-devices.py, settings-network.py, settings-sharing.py, settings-system.py, settings-accounts.py, settings-time.py, settings-apps.py, settings-privacy.py. Each runs twice:
  - `tools/heavy.sh --min-mb 2560 --tag <batch> -- python3 -B tests/gnome/harness.py launch run --lang nl --scenario tests/gnome/scenarios/settings-<x>.py`
  - the same with `--lang en --out tests/gnome/scenarios/settings-<x>.en.out`
  - with --strace whenever a page can reach pkexec, systemctl, passwd, nmcli or grdctl.
- Each scenario, per page:
  1. Opens it with h.open('settings:<id>'). Data pages are reached by clicking through the parent, using h.settings_data_page, because their title is the item's name.
  2. Takes h.screenshot('<id>.nl' or '<id>.en').
  3. Checks the title, the breadcrumb chain and zero Dutch-word hits in en.
  4. Flips every bound control by its st-<page>-<key> widget name with real pointer clicks, then reads the private keyfile with h.gsettings_get and requires GNOME's exact value. Mouse is the reference case: left-handed true, speed 0.5 from slider position 15, accel-profile flat, natural-scroll true.
  5. Writes the key from outside with h.gsettings_set and requires the switch to follow (gsettings.changed).
  6. Locks a key in the keyfile and requires the lock state; checks that a WinPoint-owned key shows its pointer instead of a switch.
  7. For polkit actions: the stand-in receives the call with interactive=true. Where GNOME's helper is used, the run/stubs pkexec log shows the exact argv and the strace exec check shows that no real pkexec, apt, PackageKit client or python3 ran from a WinPoint process. Orca and IBus preferences must appear as gnome-shell children.
  8. Hardware-dependent pages (touchpad, pen, usb, mobile, fingerprint, colour sensor) stay hidden without their stand-in or caps fixture and appear with it.
- Mirror checks in settings-system.py and settings-time.py: DND in Settings changes show-banners and the shell flyout's state; the flyout's DND changes show-banners; clock-format, seconds and weekday reach the taskbar clock text; battery percentage reaches the tray.
- Regression guard: native-shell.py, native-gtk-apps.py and lock-unlock.py still pass, and `win11-app --gnome-look` in a GNOME-mode run restores accent-color with the existing look keys. Nothing a batch writes appears in the Ubuntu-only schemas.
- Integration runs settings-tour.py: every registry page in nl and en, screenshots kept locally (PNGs gitignored like the other .out dirs, results.json committed), no unknown_method, no placeholder, no error toast on an idle page, memory within the native-gtk-apps budget.
